newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemalan volcano erupts, villagers evacuated.
newsitem.headline: Guatemalan volcano erupts, villagers evacuated.

text.p: A volcano erupted with rare strength south of the Guatemalan capital on Friday, spewing streams of lava and forcing the immediate evacuation of nearby villages, authorities said.
There were no deaths or injuries immediately reported.
"It is throwing out rivers of lava and a thick column of ash," Eddy Sanchez, director of the National Seismology Institute, told Reuters by telephone.
He said the eruption occured at midnight on the Pacaya volcano, some 20 miles (32 kms) south of the capital. He described it as the biggest eruption there since 1987.
In Guatemala City, awe-struck residents could see fiery explosions shooting from the volcano top lighting up the midnight sky.
Sanchez said there were no reports of injuries or deaths, but as a precaution emergency workers were evacuating El Patrocinio, a town of 700 inhabitants, and other towns on the volcano's flanks.
Pacaya is one of several active volcanos studded across Guatemala, and it erupts regularly. But fire officials said these were the biggest explosions they had seen in years.
